title: Adaptive focus outlines and brand elevation harmonization for dense surfaces
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: As the Console onboarding of new brand palettes increased, we observed inconsistent focus outlines and elevation perception across dense UIs (data tables, compact lists, and chart overlays). Some brand colors collapse the focus ring against semi-opaque surfaces in dark modes, and elevation interplay causes actionable borders to become indistinguishable at small sizes. This ticket scopes design system changes to establish adaptive focus outlines and a harmonized elevation overlay strategy that works across brand themes and both light/dark modes.

Goals: (1) Define a small set of focus-outline styles that adapt by surface depth and brand luminance so keyboard navigation remains visible without overpowering micro-interactions. (2) Introduce a composable elevation overlay token that blends with brand accents to preserve contrast for borders, shadows, and chart axis strokes. (3) Provide component-level override guidelines for tables, buttons, and chart axes to remain legible when theme-branding is applied.

Why now: This reduces accessibility regressions reported by beta customers using custom brand palettes and reduces engineering rework for ad-hoc overrides.

Scope: core tokens (focus-outline, elevation-overlay), component adaptors for TableRow, CompactButton, MiniChip, ChartAxis, and Legend; update dev docs and Figma kit. Excludes runtime implementation (separate ENG ticket).
acceptance_criteria: A1: Three focus-outline variants (subtle, standard, prominent) are defined with clear algorithmic rules based on surface depth and brand luminance.
A2: An elevation-overlay token family (overlay-1..overlay-4) is specified with blending recipes for light and dark base surfaces.
A3: Component adaptation guidelines for TableRow, CompactButton, and ChartAxis are documented with example overrides for two sample brand palettes.
A4: Figma components updated and published to the design library; dev-facing spec doc added with visual examples and CSS token names.
A5: Accessibility tests: keyboard focus remains >3:1 contrast against background for standard/principal focus variants when applied with sample brand colors.
A6: Hand-off checklist completed (Figma links, tokens.json mapping, dev notes) and a prototyping playground link included.
design_notes: We prefer a small composable system vs. per-component bespoke rules to keep engineering surface area low.
Focus-outline should be a stroke around the component's interactive bounding box where possible; for densely packed controls, use an inner-glow variant to avoid layout shifts.
Elevation-overlay will be implemented as an additive semi-opaque layer (rgba) with a multiply/lighten blending fallback for older renderers.
Chart axes and thin strokes should use a derived contrastStroke token that samples from axis-contrast-or-accent depending on visibility needs.
Provide a fallback neutral-outline when brand luminance is within 10% of the surface to avoid washed-out rings.
Avoid increasing absolute line widths; prefer contrast and layering adjustments to preserve compact density.
Include explicit guidance for disabled state (muted focus) and motion-reduced variants.
Prototyping note: build an interactive Figma variant with toggles for brand A/B and light/dark to validate edge cases.
Coordinate with ENG: runtime token names must be token.focus.subtle | token.focus.standard | token.focus.prominent and overlay.elev-1..elev-4.
decisions: Use three focus variants instead of adaptive per-component selectors to limit token proliferation.
Adopt an overlay-based elevation model (overlay.elev-1..4) rather than per-component shadows for consistent cross-brand behavior.
For charts, prioritize axis readability: axis stroke uses contrastStroke derived token; legend uses a separate legend-contrast token to avoid color clashes.
Defer theme builder automation for brand luminance sampling to a follow-up eng initiative; initial guidance will include static threshold rules.
Accessibility threshold chosen: WCAG 2.1 AA (3:1) for focus visibility on non-text UI components (consistent with internal accessibility policy).
Inner-glow focus variant used for very dense rows (table compact density) to avoid layout overflow when focus appears.
Fallback neutral-outline token will be used for brand colors that fail contrast checks; designers should only opt into prominent focus for critical controls.
Design tokens will be published as plain name mappings (no nested objects) to match Linear doc schema for easy handoff.
